key_insight: EDA-L2D adapts when to defer AI decisions to humans by modeling changes in expert reliability over time.
clinical_relevance: For medical diagnosis workflows, adaptive deferral could help allocate cases between AI and clinicians as human performance fluctuates.
method: Uses a sequence model to encode recent expert outcomes.
Conditions the deferral head on this history to track reliability shifts.
Adapts decision allocation between human and machine over time.
evidence_signal: Experiments across image classification, medical diagnosis, and hate speech detection report improved system performance over prior L2D methods, including under irregular expert-reliability shifts.
watch_item: Deployment depends on obtaining timely, reliable expert-outcome feedback; the abstract does not establish prospective clinical benefit.
paper_title: Learning to Defer under Expert Drift
